input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The check was changed from `isinstance(filename, str)` to `isinstance(filename, os.PathLike)`, so a plain `str` filename is no longer wrapped in a tuple.
- rationale: Trigger: `click.edit(filename="file.txt")`, the most common usage. A str is not an os.PathLike, so it is passed to edit_files as an iterable of characters. The editor is then launched with one argument per character instead of the single file. The check should be `isinstance(filename, (str, os.PathLike))`.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: the isinstance check now tests only os.PathLike, so a plain str is not wrapped in a tuple. It also gives the same consequence: the string is iterated character by character, and the editor is launched with one argument per character.
